Maria: quick sync — I kicked off a side-by-side: replay-harness vs tuned-synthetic across two kernels (fast-attn-v2, matmul-fused) with KV cache toggled. Early flag: matmul-fused + kvcache shows ~1.9x TPOT slowdown vs fast-attn-v2. want to lock down methodology before we chase kernel changes.
Ashwin: thanks. paste the harness configs + exact metric defs. people often mix up TTFT vs TPOT when they interpret p95s.
Maria: ok. measurement defs first: TTFT = time(request accepted -> first token emitted). TPOT = time(first token -> last token emitted). per-request p50/p95/p99 computed on raw TTFT and TPOT. Goodput = total_tokens_emitted / wall_clock_time (exclude failed reqs). QPS = accepted_requests / wall_clock_time. I used per-request CSVs to recompute percentiles.
Maria: harness snippet I used:
```
runner: replay-harness
trace: prod-sample-2025-12
client_pacing: replay-original
kernel: matmul-fused
kvcache: enabled
continuous_batching: true
batch_target: 64
batch_aging_ms: 10
pad_policy: token-aligned
metrics: ttft, tpot, ttft_p50/p95/p99, tpot_p50/p95/p99, goodput, qps, kv_hit_rate
warmup: 10k_tokens_per_client
```
Jordyn: important: apples-to-apples requires matching arrival jitter + seq-length CDF. replay is already correct but synthetic must be fitted to the trace CDF (p50/75/95 lengths) otherwise the batching envelope differs and you get different kernel launch patterns.
Eva: are we seeing the 1.9x on TPOT only or end-to-end including queueing? and which percentile moves most?
Maria: mostly TPOT. breakdown: p50 ~1.0x, p95 ~1.7x, p99 ~1.9x. queueing was small because I limited concurrency, so tail is in token emission. profiler flame indicates matmul-fused spends more time in kv_lookup loop with kvcache enabled (~20% token time), while fast-attn-v2 shows higher steady per-token compute but less kv contention.
bench-bot: profiling summary (auto): matmul-fused: kv_lookup hot-path increased; lock hold time visible. fast-attn-v2: higher kernel-launch overhead but stable per-token latency.
Ashwin: possible hot mutex in kvcache combined with matmul reorder. did you run with lock-debug build or trace locks? continuous_batching is on — that interaction has bitten us before.
Maria: yes continuous_batching=true. tried batch_aging_ms=5/10/20 — TPOT delta <5% for matmul-fused. suspect conditional path triggered by kvcache misses aligning to batch boundaries.
Jordyn: can we validate per-batch kv_hit_rate distribution? if some batches have mixed hit/miss patterns we can get slow-path serialization and tail amplification.
Sam: propose experiment matrix:
- replay-harness (baseline)
- synthetic tuned to trace CDF + jitter
- synthetic naive (mismatched lengths)
For each: run kernels = fast-attn-v2, matmul-fused, matmul-fused(lock-debug). collect per-request CSVs, per-batch kv_hit_rate, kernel_launch_time, gpu_busy%, and TTFT/TPOT raw samples.
Maria: good. add pre-warm vs post-warm: run warmup 10k tokens/client then measure; also capture ttft_tail_breakdown (queue_wait, kernel_exec, io) per request.
bench-bot: load run scheduled -> id perf-226001-01, start 2026-03-18T15:05:12Z
Maria: I'll run 3x30m experiments on perf-rig (4xA100). will post run ids + raw CSVs here. reminder: include kernel build hash and commit in metadata so we don't chase unrelated regressions.
Ashwin: when you post results, include raw per-request CSVs. recomputing p99 from aggregated buckets caused the last false positive.
Eva: also capture sequence-length CDF and batch size distribution per-run — those explain batching differences.
Maria: will include table in summary: {run_id, runner_type, kernel, kvcache, qps, avg_tokens_per_req, goodput, ttft_p95, tpot_p95, kv_hit_rate_p50/p95, kernel_launch_p95}
Jordyn: and include a short script to recompute percentiles from CSV so reviewers can verify.
Sam: tagging eng-runtime for visibility. :eyes:
Maria: thanks all — kicking off now. will report back with links to artifacts and a 1-paragraph conclusion per run.
